newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel bonds rise, unaffected by Iraq conflict.
newsitem.headline: Israel bonds rise, unaffected by Iraq conflict.

text.p: * Consumer price index (CPI) linked bonds: +0.3 pct to 163.01
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills : +0.06 pct to 155.31
The bond market closed up, unaffected by the U.S. missile attacks against Iraq, traders said.

"Trading today was very positive with prices rising from 0.2 percent to 0.5 percent, which is a lot for one day. The crisis (between the United States and Iraq) has not affected trade," said Roy Mayer of Simodan portfolio managers.
"Turnover was relatively low at 83 million shekels and demand for bonds was close to 300 million shekels," he said.

Mayer said the demand was from commercial banks who need to invest the large sums of money flowing into their savings plans from the public. But sellers are scarce because provident funds, who until recently had been dumping bonds, have stopped selling.
"The atmosphere in the CPI-linked bonds (which were the ones provident funds were dumping) is much better (than before)."
One trader said, "Today was the third day of trade where we noticed a significant fall in yields of fixed-rate CPI-linked bonds."

"In August these yields were 5.6 percent for six-year bonds, while for 15-year bonds yields were at 5.25 percent. Today the yield curve has fallen significantly and returns on the six-year bonds are 5.2 percent and on the 15-year bonds 5.1 percent," he said.
Mayer said he did not know if the positive trading marked a turnaround. "We have to see if the massive public redemptions from provident funds continue," he said.
Israel's low stock and bond prices have affected the performance of provident funds, triggering public redemptions. Provident funds are long-term savings funds with special tax benefits.
The central bank has bought government bonds to stop prices from falling further. Traders say the purchases have temporarily brought respite to the market.
- Shoshanna Solomon, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 SAS TCC
